description: co-develop generic dev spine hub suite — batch D of the 2026-11-01-hub-consolidation Phase 1, the SEMANTIC-MERGE batch for the generic development spine (agents architect/code-writer/test-runner + skills code-review/refactoring/test-driven-development). The six canonicals in templates/co-develop are authored merge products per the batch C mechanism: hub-promotion's byte-identity asset model would overwrite them with the unparameterized Projects/co-develop L3 bytes, so all six are registry-only rows here. Authoring decisions: (a) agents keep the L2 [Project Name] scaffold token the template copies already carry and parameterize measured per-spoke body deltas with {{PROJECT_IMPLEMENTATION_AGENT}} (architect, test-runner — co-game binds game-developer) and {{PROJECT_AUDIT_COMMAND}} (test-runner — co-game binds bash scripts/audit.sh); frontmatter handoff_to/handoff_from/required_skills stay single-valued co-develop doctrine with per-spoke bindings documented in a Spoke Derivation Note; all three agents bumped 1.1.1 -> 1.2.0 (code-writer note-only — it IS the implementation role, no tokens). (b) SKILLS stay at their measured on-disk versions (code-review 1.0.1, refactoring 1.0.1, test-driven-development 1.0.0; last_reviewed unchanged): these three are multi-variant at L2 (co-develop + co-game templates) and the Variant-Exclusive catalog gate fails any one-sided version bump — the minor bump to 1.1.0 lands with the co-game re-derivation wave, when both variants move together; this batch's skill changes are body-only (Spoke Derivation Note added; refactoring additionally drops the stray '", ' EOF artifact carried by all four pre-consolidation copies). (c) assets[] carries the only byte-clean suite-coupled files — the three lifecycle reference cards (byte-identical L3<->L2 re-assert, zero-overwrite). EXCLUSIONS per the batch scope: agent stack-setup and agent designer are present in only 2/16 projects (co-develop, co-game) — fan-in data does not prove them generic, so they stay OUT of the spine (their known_unregistered_duplicates soak rows remain); co-abap's abap-code-review is domain-specific. Consumer-set corrections vs the fleet-report fanIn2 evidence: co-learning is NOT an installed consumer of refactoring/test-driven-development/code-review (its skill-graph projection carries only dangling reference nodes with content_hash null for the first two, and it never carried code-review on disk), so consumers[] records co-game only for the three skills; co-learning IS a real consumer of all three agents (installed 1.0.0 copies, next-wave re-derivation); co-abap is excluded from every consumer set — its three agents are SAP-specific forks, not derivations of this doctrine. Tokens join PLACEHOLDER_ALLOWLIST (upgrade-policy.ts v1.36.0, both schema copies of the script); the six registered assets retire their known_unregistered_duplicates soak rows in the same commit.
